node-1.label: A young woman in her mid-to-late teens presented with a 3-month history of protruding eyes, blurred vision, and chronic frontal headache

node-2.label: History of acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosed at age 9, with 2 central nervous system relapses at ages 12 and 16

node-3.label: Physical examination: corrected visual acuity 6/12, pinhole 6/9 in both eyes; Hertel exophthalmometry 25 mm bilaterally on base 105; pupils slightly sluggish without relative afferent defect; both optic discs grossly swollen; intraocular pressure and eye movements normal

why.why: The prior ALL history with repeated CNS relapses and bilateral proptosis/optic disc swelling already suggested leukemic relapse. New imaging evidence showing progressive orbital roof scalloping and medial wall displacement indicates orbital leukemic infiltration, and CSF blast count of 1400×10^6/L with elevated opening pressure confirms leptomeningeal relapse. Pathologist and radiologist analyses both interpret these as confirmatory for leukemic orbital/CNS relapse, so confidence is raised from 0.85 to 0.96.

Although headache, blurred vision, and optic disc swelling overlap with raised intracranial pressure, the new CSF blast count of 1400×10^6/L and imaging evidence of progressive orbital bone scalloping/medial wall displacement indicate malignant infiltration rather than primary IIH. The elevated opening pressure is explained by leptomeningeal leukemic involvement, and the ALL relapse history makes IIH very unlikely, so confidence is reduced from 0.1 to 0.02.

Proptosis could superficially mimic orbital inflammation, but imaging shows progressive scalloping/destruction of the orbital walls with medial wall displacement, and the CSF blast count of 1400×10^6/L confirms leukemic infiltration. The pathologist analysis excludes infection or inflammatory pseudotumor, and the ALL relapse history strongly favors malignant relapse, so confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.01.
